text:
alex: Thinking about on-prem bundle lifecycle: how do we safely GC blobs when customers apply many deltas offline?
sophia: We need a compact snapshot mechanism that marks a GC-safe manifest state. Without it GC is scary.
marcus: Proposal: add a compact-snapshot artifact that contains a manifest of live blobs + a snapshot-hash signed by operator. GC only allowed when snapshot-hash matches local state.
lee: Important: snapshot creation must be operator-initiated and require a preflight that verifies runtime compatibility. No automatic GC.
alex: Agreed. Also we should record a compact-snapshot id in activation metadata so resume/rollback logic can reference it.
sophia: For air-gapped installs, operator signatures are common (GPG). Support both operator-signed snapshots and sealed-snapshot mode (sealed by central signer but validated later).
marcus: Sealed-snapshot mode: agent accepts snapshot but marks state as quarantine until remote validation arrives. Telemetry flag for number of sealed snapshots pending.
lee: UX: `redwood-gc --snapshot <id> --force` with explicit human prompt and a 24h delayed window by default. Also show `redwood-snapshot --dry-run` that lists candidate blobs.
ops-bot: integration-test job #9021: compact-snapshot roundtrip failed on rhel8 due to path normalization :warning:
alex: We'll add canonical path rules in manifest proto (utf-8, trimmed, sorted). Also include a blob reference count as optional field for quick checks.
sophia: Follow-up RFC should include: manifest additions, snapshot lifecycle, GC playbook, agent flags for sealed vs operator-signed, and simple CLI UX.
marcus: I can prototype snapshot verifier lib to avoid agent/host skew. Will include examples for GPG and PEM verification.
lee: Ping @eng-sre and @product-security when RFC is ready. Sync Thurs 10am to review failure modes.
